I did trade the S23U in for the S24U to get a flat display, as I hate curved ones, but nothing here adds value. Battery life on the S24U is two days for me, performance is overkill, the display is Grade A, it is smooth, and it has performed with very few issues over the year. The cameras are above average with pros and cons, but no perfect camera phone exists. This is very expensive for those not trading in, coming from much older devices, but it would likely be a fantastic long-term buy. But then again, there are cheaper, similarly excellent phones in Europe that I can say the same for, so if I were buying now, I would probably buy the Honor Magic 7 Pro at £350 less or the OP13 with a free watch for a similar saving.

This movie shows that, despite appearing that the emotions have full control over their person, the reality is that they only serve as guides/managers of the mind. This is seen in how Riley, as she started entering puberty, develops her sense of self, which allows her to take her own decisions without the influence of her own emotions. This is shown in many moments: Riley remembering memories that the emotions didn't call up, like the penalty she committed during a hockey game. Anxiety being unable to force Riley to join the opposite team to her best friend's because of that being against her beliefs. Even after Joy was able to replace the Sense of Self created by Anxiety with the old one and take the latter from the console, Riley's anxiety attack continued, only stopping when Joy allowed a new Sense of Self (created from both good and bad beliefs) to emerge and she and the other emotions comforted Riley. Riley was able to choose to experience Joy, after her anxiety attack ended and she managed to make up with her best friends.

A rare comment from me to explain why this stunt is actually 100% real and give people a better appreciation of this video. Rewatch this a few times after you read my post. 1) The trucks are driven in reverse for two reasons. People who've driven anything with a trailer know how difficult it is to keep it completely steady in reverse. The secondary reason is there's less possibility of JCVD being run over, if he were to have fallen off. 2) The trucks are _NOT_ identical. The truck on the left of the video is 3 axled and the truck on the right is 5 axled. What this means is the truck on the left is a box truck, while the truck on the right is a truck + trailer. This is important as it explains why the truck on the left is the one that moves. If you turn while reversing a trailer, the trailer WILL turn in the opposite direction. This means if the truck on the right had done the spreading, the trailer would have moved closer to the other truck and made the stunt impossible. If you want to try this in real life...push and pull a kids wagon or a pallet jack while turning. You'll understand why this is so significant. 3) There are 4 people you can see in the trucks. Two of them are watching the solid lines to understand spacing. The other two are observing the dotted lines...notice the right truck occasionally has a white spot show up near the right side of the right truck. The dotted lines and spots are used by the other two people to gauge their timing/speed. This is an absolutely amazing and creative stunt. Hats off to whoever designed the stunt in it's entirety; they really thought it out.
